$comment: The /playground demo roster. Hand-authored, and reconciled BOTH DIRECTIONS against the rendered route by check:features, on the content/features.json and content/projects.json precedent. A demo here that the page does not render is a lie in the manifest; a demo the page renders that is absent here is an unindexed section. The enum value sets are deliberately restated here so the gate can argue them against the module that owns them (CHART_TYPES in app/lib/content/chart.mjs, RRF_K in app/lib/search/query.mjs): two sources that must agree, not one source copied.

$swatchComment: Ratified palette pairs the contrast lab opens on, and the gate's behavioural fixtures. They live here rather than in the route so check:features can compute the expected ratio through app/lib/contrast.mjs and compare it against the pair the page actually offers. A pair here that the page does not render, or a preset on the page that is not here, fails reconciliation.
$datasetComment: The chart demo's fixed datasets. REAL RECORDED DATA, per the chart directive's own rule: both are lifted from measurements already published on this site. They live here rather than in the route so the gate renders the identical SVG through app/lib/content/chart.mjs. The keys must equal the chart demo's dataset enum, asserted both directions.

limiter.label: Rate limiter, three mechanisms
limiter.title: Requests allowed against the ceiling each mechanism was given
limiter.alt: Comparison of allowed requests against the ceiling for three rate limiting mechanisms. The GA ratelimit binding allowed 11 against a limit of 5. A Durable Object using async storage allowed 8 against a ceiling of 3. A Durable Object using the synchronous SQLite API allowed exactly 3 against a ceiling of 3.
limiter.csv:
mechanism,allowed,ceiling
GA ratelimit,11,5
async DO storage,8,3
sync SQLite DO,3,3
limiter.note: Categorical x, two series. The x scale is a band and the series take the first two colours of the chart ladder.

corpus.label: Search corpus growth
corpus.title: Search records against published posts
corpus.alt: Search index size against post count at four recorded points: 7 records from 1 post, 47 from 6 posts, 84 from 11 posts and 93 from 12 posts. Records grow faster than posts because each heading is indexed separately.
corpus.note: Numeric x, one series. Every x value parses as a number, so the scale is inferred as linear rather than a band.
